subject: ss-infectious-diseases
title: Beta-lactams and beta-lactamase inhibitors: choosing therapy against resistant gram-negatives

steps.tx: Beta-lactams kill bacteria by binding penicillin-binding proteins and blocking cell wall cross-linking. Their main threat is **beta-lactamase**, an enzyme that opens the beta-lactam ring. **Beta-lactamase inhibitors** protect the antibiotic by binding the enzyme, so the partner drug survives. Classic inhibitors such as clavulanate, sulbactam and tazobactam act as suicide inhibitors. Newer agents, avibactam, vaborbactam and relebactam, block carbapenemases and some class A and C enzymes.

steps.tx: Stratify the infection first. **Localised** disease, such as uncomplicated cystitis, is different from **systemic** disease, such as urosepsis, pneumonia, bacteraemia or septic shock. Resistance is graded as multidrug-resistant, extensively drug-resistant or pandrug-resistant. Choose therapy by the resistance mechanism: ESBL producers usually need a carbapenem, while carbapenemase producers need a newer combination.

rows: Avoid ceftriaxone and piperacillin-tazobactam for serious disease
Third-generation cephalosporins may fail during therapy
Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam if aztreonam-avibactam unavailable

steps.tx: Know the intrinsic gaps. **Proteus**, **Morganella** and **Providencia** are less susceptible to imipenem, so a carbapenem does not cover every Enterobacterales. Tetracyclines and polymyxins are poorly active against the Proteeae and Serratia, and may not reach adequate urine or blood levels. Avoid relying on third-generation cephalosporins for AmpC producers such as Enterobacter cloacae and Citrobacter freundii, because resistance can emerge during treatment.

steps.tx: Penicillin allergy is labelled far more often than it is real. Around **8 to 10 percent** of United States patients report it. A structured score such as **PEN-FAST** helps risk-stratify. A score above 3 signals higher probability of true IgE-mediated allergy. Diagnosis uses history, skin testing and graded challenge where appropriate. Cross-reactivity depends mainly on the R side chain rather than the beta-lactam ring, so dissimilar side chains are safer.

right.title: Low-risk or absolute avoid
points: Isolated remote hives may allow delabelling

steps.tx: Recognise anaphylaxis early. Give intramuscular **epinephrine 0.3 mg** into the mid-anterolateral thigh without waiting for a serum tryptase. Repeat every 5 minutes if hypotension persists. Isolated hives, without systemic features, are treated with an oral H1 antihistamine such as cetirizine. Biphasic reactions and mortality are linked to delayed epinephrine, so timing matters.

steps.tx: Watch for neurotoxicity and organ toxicity. High-dose penicillin in **renal impairment** can cause myoclonus, altered mental status and seizures. The first step is stopping the drug. Prolonged therapy needs renal, hepatic and haematological monitoring. Piperacillin-tazobactam can cause thrombocytopenia, which matters in patients on warfarin. Severe cutaneous reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome or DRESS are a lifelong reason to avoid the class.
